steps: Check & prepare the existing fireplace

Opening at least 23-1/2" H × 33-1/2" front W × 16-3/8" D × 24-1/2" back W; chimney non-combustible, clean, 10'–50' tall. Block the damper open or remove it, remove the chimney cap, and attach the conversion warning label at the bottom of the firebox.

Approved for solid-fuel masonry and factory-built fireplaces. Complete all of section 5.0 before installing.

  • Opening minimums: 23-1/2" (597mm) high, 33-1/2" (851mm) front width, 16-3/8" (419mm) deep, 24-1/2" (622mm) back width.
  • Chimney: masonry 6" × 8" min I.D. or factory-built solid fuel 7" min I.D.; 10' (3m) to 50' (15.24m) tall; non-combustible, clean and in good working order. Clean the chimney and fireplace to keep creosote odor out of the home. Chimney clean-outs must fit properly.
  • Flue damper fully blocked open or removed; remove the existing chimney cap.
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails and mesh, and log grates may be removed. Removed parts must be re-installable if the insert is ever removed (removing rivets or screws is acceptable). No cutting of sheet metal parts.
  • Gas line must be able to reach the insert: access hole on the right side. If a factory-built firebox has none, a hole of 1½" (37.5mm) or less may be drilled through the lower sides or bottom, then plugged with non-combustible insulation after the line is in.
  • Provide electrical power to the insert, and verify mantel and sidewall clearances (section 8.0).
  • Mechanically attach the conversion warning label at the bottom of the existing firebox so it's visible if the insert is removed.
Cut & attach liners to the cap

Measure fireplace base to chimney top, subtract the insert height, and cut the #816 3" flex to that length. Intake (end without collar) over cap collar A; exhaust (red marking) sealed onto collar B; 3 screws each, exhaust collar on the right.

1. Measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney (easier with two people) and subtract the insert height: that's the co-linear flex length. Cut #816 (36' / 10.97m of 3" flexible pipe) to it.
  2. Carefully extend the exhaust and combustion air intake pipes to that length.
  3. Slide the combustion air intake pipe (the end without a collar) over cap collar A; secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).
  4. Run a bead of sealant around the inner edge of the exhaust pipe end (without collar, red marking), slide it onto collar B, secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided) and seal around the joint.

Install the cap with the exhaust collar on the right; the insert's exhaust collar is on the right too. Horizontal runs: 24" (609mm) max, with a 1" (25mm) rise per 12" (305mm) of run. Avoid tight bends that can abrade or damage the flex.
Run liners & set the cap

Lower both 3" × 3" flex pipes down the chimney (one weighted rope per pipe if there are offsets, never one rope around both), seal and set the cap, then pull both pipes into the firebox. Insulating the liners is recommended against cold drafts.

1. Optional: wrap the first 3' (914mm) below the cap with unfaced insulation; secure with wire.
  2. If the chimney has offsets, put a weighted rope around each pipe end to guide it. Don't tie one rope around both pipes.
  3. Install the 3" × 3" flexible pipes down through the chimney.
  4. Run a liberal bead of sealant around the top of the chimney and set the cap per the vent manufacturer's manual. #816-CAP option: fasten with 2" (50mm) self-tapping screws and anchor straps (not provided) through the pilot holes on its sides.
  5. From inside the fireplace, pull the ropes or pipes down until both the exhaust and intake pipes are in the firebox.
  6. Optional: to prevent heat loss up the chimney, place unfaced insulation between the flex pipes and the chimney.

Hussong recommends insulating the flex pipes and chimney with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136 to prevent cold air drafts.
Connect liners to the vent adapter

Slide the vent adapter back out of its channels on top of the insert. Exhaust (red marking) inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', intake over the intake collar, each with sealant and (3) ½" self-tapping screws, then seal the joints airtight.

1. Remove the vent adapter from the top of the insert by sliding it back out of its channels.
  2. Place the adapter in the existing fireplace opening.
  3. Exhaust: bead of sealant around the pipe (red marking), slide it inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', secure with (3) ½ in (13mm) self-tapping screws, then seal around the joint.
  4. Intake: liberal bead of sealant around the intake collar, slide the combustion intake pipe over it, secure with (3) ½ in (13mm) self-tapping screws, then seal around the joint.
  5. Visually check both connections.
Each pipe must go to its correct collar at both the termination cap and the vent adapter for the insert to operate properly.
Place, seat & level the insert

Slide the insert in until its top channels align with the adapter, then push the insert in while pulling the adapter forward with the pull rod until seated. Secure with (2) ½" sheet metal screws and level with the leveling bolts (2 each side).

1. Slide the insert into the opening until the channels on top align with the vent adapter.
  2. Put the pull rod handle through the access slot on top and hook it through the hole in the pull rod. Push the insert in while pulling the vent adapter forward until seated.
  3. Secure the adapter through the slots on top with (2) ½ in (13mm) sheet metal screws (components packet).
  4. Use the pull rod handle to pull the vent adapter back to starting position; remove the handle and verify the vent connection.
  5. If needed, level the insert with the leveling bolts (components packet) threaded into the nuts on the bottom, 2 each side.
Gas line + leak check

Ships for natural gas; fit the propane kit first if needed. Run the line through the right-side access hole, clear of the fan, to a listed ½" tee-handle shut-off and flexible connector on the ½" control valve inlet; check all connections with soapy water.

• Qualified person only, to local codes (or ANSI Z223.1); in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • A listed ½" (13mm) tee-handle manual shut-off valve and flexible gas connector connect to the ½" (13mm) control valve inlet. The fireplace comes with a 3/8" (10mm) × 18" (457mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve.
  • Run the line preferably through the right gas line hole, to where the shut-off and flex line connect. Don't run it where it would obstruct fan operation.
  • At minimum opening sizes, the line may need to be run after the insert is placed.
  • Pressure testing the supply piping: above ½ psi (3.5 kPa), disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve; at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water.
Shroud & safety barrier

Lift out the upper and lower louvers and remove the glass, fasten the shroud to the cabinet's mounting nuts with (4) truss head screws, and refit. Hang the safety barrier's tabs in the shroud's 4 slots. Trim must not seal ventilation or draft relief openings.

1. Lift the upper louver up and out of its mounting slots; lift the lower louver out of the slots on its mounting bracket.
  2. Remove the glass assembly.
  3. Align the shroud's mounting holes with the mounting nuts on the sides of the cabinet (2 each side); secure with (4) truss head screws (provided).
  4. Reinstall everything removed.
  5. Safety barrier: align the tabs on its back with the 4 shroud slots (2 each side), raise it slightly into the slots and let the tabs lower into position.
  • Trim panels or surrounds must not seal ventilation openings in the existing fireplace; draft relief openings must not be covered or blocked.
  • CK34-LMK low mantel kit (CK34-PSF or CK34-RSF barriers only): remove (2) screws at the back of the screen front, slide the heat deflector under the mounting tabs, replace the screws. The gasket must contact the shroud.
  • Safety barriers need the bottom of the fireplace level with the finished hearth.
Light kit & glass media

Convert to propane first if needed. With power disconnected, install the (6) halogen bulbs under the burner cover (never bare-handed), then spread 12 lbs. (5.4 kg) of #212 or #312 glass media one layer deep, keeping the pilot clear.

Light kit (power disconnected)

  1. Remove the (8) burner cover screws and lift out the cover.
  2. Loosen, don't remove, the (4) light bar screws; slide the bars away from the screws and tip them up to expose the lamp bases.
  3. Install the (6) halogen bulbs (components packet), handled with a soft cloth, never bare hands.
  4. Re-secure the light bars and reinstall the burner cover.

Glass media: 12 lbs. (5.4 kg)

  • #212 Series crushed glass or #312 Series reflective glass, installed onto the burner assembly and pilot shield. It may be washed first; don't substitute materials.
  • One layer deep across the firebox. Never block the pilot assembly: a blocked pilot may cause delayed ignition.
  • Propane with #212: remove 50% or more of the media covering the burner ports for proper flame appearance.
  • Save unused media for later.
Note: on media coverage, p. 28 says to install the media onto the burner assembly and pilot shield (and, for propane, to remove 50% or more of the media covering the burner ports), then in the next step says the media must not cover any part of the burner.
Power up & initialize the control

Rocker switch OFF, (4) AA in the backup holder, (3) AAA in the remote, plug in. Clear the firebox, press red SW1 (3 beeps, amber LED), press remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps, pilot lights), press it again (pilot out), then rocker switch ON.

1. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF.
  2. Install (4) AA batteries (not included) in the backup battery holder on the control module, and (3) AAA batteries (components packet) in the remote.
  3. Connect the IFC module to AC power: a properly grounded three-prong receptacle, hot at all times, with no switch in the supply.
  4. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox. The next steps start the pilot igniter, and the pilot lights if gas is supplied.
  5. Press the red SW1 button on the IFC module: 3 beeps and an amber LED (ready to sync).
  6. Within 5 seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: 4 beeps, and the pilot lights.
  7. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out, confirming the command. The system is initialized.
  8. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote control operation.

Pilot mode (IPI or CPI) is chosen on the remote with the system off: Mode to the CPI icon, Up for CPI, Down for IPI.
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet (IN tap) and manifold (OUT tap) pressures with a manometer on a ¼" I.D. hose, then confirm both taps reseal. Flames start blue and turn lazy yellow over the first 15 minutes; venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician only.

Inlet NG / LP5" – 10.5" / 12" – 13" WC
Manifold NG / LP1.1" – 3.8" / 2.9" – 11" WC
Venturi factory openingNG 1/8" (3mm) · LP 5/8" (16mm)

Test inlet pressure with all other gas appliances in the house on; test manifold pressure at the OUT tap with the burner lit. After each test, snug the tap screw (don't over-tighten) and confirm the tap reads no pressure.

Flame appearance (p. 38)

Blue at first light, gradually turning yellow over the first 15 minutes; the goal is lazy, yellow flames. Small venturi changes have dramatic results: burn at least 15 minutes and let the unit cool between adjustments.

  • Dark orange with black tips: venturi closed too far, open it slightly.
  • Soot on the glass: improper media placement, venturi setting (open slightly), or vent cap installation or blockage (p. 40).
Note: on which way to set the venturi for blue or lifting flames, the manual says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and Table 12.4 says to close it slightly for short, blue flames (p. 38); but Table 12.4 also blames lifting (ghosting) flames on a venturi closed too far (open slightly, or gas pressure too high), and the troubleshooting chart says to open the shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner (p. 40).

panels.title: Pilot won't light or stay lit
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power, or use battery backup with fully charged batteries
Wiring disconnected → check every connection against the wiring schematic
Gas supply off → check every shut-off; there may be more than one between appliance and main line
No propane, or low gas pressure (bent line, too-narrow pipe, low line pressure) → refill tank; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot flame not enveloping the flame sensor → adjust the pilot screw on the valve (clockwise smaller, counterclockwise larger), then seal it

panels.title: Main burner won't light
items: ON/OFF rocker switch OFF → switch it ON
Gas supply off or low → check all shut-offs and the propane tank; consult a plumber or gas supplier
Faulty or incorrect wiring → check and correct
Plugged main burner orifice → remove blockage
Pilot not directed to ignite the burner → see the pilot causes
Remote not working or no call for heat → replace batteries; remote ON, thermostat OFF
No reaction to commands → replace batteries, reprogram the remote to the IFC module, or reset the IFC after too many failed ignitions

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out while running
items: Glass assembly installed incorrectly → refit per section 9.1
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Exhaust pipe leaking exhaust back into the firebox → find and repair leaks

panels.title: Soot on the glass
items: Improper media placement → redo per section 9.3
Venturi setting → open the air shutter slightly (12.2.1)
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris

codes: Pack under 4V; low double-beep on ON/OFF. Replace the AA batteries.
No flame after 2 tries. Verify gas is on and the sensor isn't shorted; reset, or re-initialize (11.2).

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your insert lights itself: an igniter sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Every day

Press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace beeps once, and about 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot. Press ON/OFF again to turn it off. For remote control, the main ON/OFF rocker switch must be set to ON.

If it doesn't light

The control makes 2 tries, sparking about 60 seconds each, with about 35 seconds between. Then it locks out, and its red light blinks 3 times at intervals. To reset, press ON/OFF to turn the system off, wait about 2 seconds, and press it again.

The full lighting steps

  1. Turn the fireplace off with the remote, then turn off all electric power to it.
  2. Turn the manual gas valve clockwise to OFF. Wait 5 minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety.
  3. If you don't, turn the valve counterclockwise to ON, turn the power back on, and turn the fireplace on with the remote.
Still won't work? Turn the fireplace off with the remote, turn the manual valve clockwise to OFF, and call your service technician or gas supplier. Turn the valve by hand only, and never use tools. If it won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it: call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

remote.title: Using the Proflame 2 remote
remote.html:
The remote takes 3 AAA batteries. A single beep from the fireplace confirms each command.

  • ON/OFF turns the fireplace on and off.
  • Up / Down arrows set the flame, with 6 levels. Down lowers it one step at a time, all the way to off. If the flame is off while the system is on, Up relights it on high.
  • Thermostat key: press once and the remote works as a room thermostat; set the temperature with the arrows. Press until SMART shows and it turns the flame down as the room reaches your setting. You can't change the flame by hand while SMART is on.
  • Mode key steps to the fan (6 speeds) and the accent light (6 levels); adjust with the arrows.

In thermostat mode the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights and runs about 12 minutes after it goes off. In manual mode it runs at its last setting, with no delay.

Handy extras

  • Key lock: press Mode and Up together; a lock icon appears. Do it again to unlock.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press Thermostat and Mode together.

sounds.title: That sound or smell is probably normal
sounds.html:
Foggy glass

When the fireplace is first lit, condensation forms on the glass. That's normal in all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time; it helps the paint cure faster.

Ticks and pings

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, so you'll hear some noise. That's normal and doesn't affect how well the fireplace works or how long it lasts.

Blue flames at first

When first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn yellow. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips (soot), the burner's air shutter may need adjusting. That's a job for a qualified service technician.

A gas smell is different. If you smell gas, don't light anything or touch any switch. Leave the building and call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The manual lists glass cleaning as a once-a-year homeowner job. Only do it when the fireplace is off and completely cool.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough to lay the glass assembly on.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. Pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom of the firebox out and down, then lift the glass assembly up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  4. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Never use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. To refit, set the slots at the top of the glass assembly over the tabs while lowering the bottom into place, then pull the latches out and up to lock it.
  6. Put the safety screen back.
Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or without the safety screen. Don't strike or slam the glass. Replacement glass comes only from Hussong Mfg. as a complete assembly, fitted by a licensed or qualified service person.

pilot.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
pilot.html:
The pilot can work two ways. You choose on the remote.

IPISpark-to-pilot: the igniter lights the pilot when you turn the fireplace on
CPIContinuous (standing) pilot that stays lit

A standing pilot keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

To switch

  1. With the system off, press Mode until the CPI icon is selected.
  2. Press Up for CPI, or Down to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms it.

With the fireplace on, a snowflake icon on the remote's screen means CPI is on.

Pilot went out by itself?

In CPI, if the main burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off. That's a standard safety feature; lighting the burner restarts the 7-day timer. The control also switches off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours of continuous pilot operation to run a safety check, then repeats your last command.

Pilot won't go out? The system is set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on household power, with a backup battery pack so it still works in a power outage.

Backup pack (control module)4 AA batteries, not included
Remote3 AAA batteries, included

During an outage

On battery backup only the burner works. The fan and lights won't run until power is back. How long the batteries last depends on things like their quality and the number of ignitions.

Low-battery signs

  • Backup pack: the fireplace gives a low double-beep when you press ON/OFF, and the red light blinks once at intervals. It won't accept commands until you replace the batteries, and it beeps once when it powers up with fresh ones.
  • Remote: a battery icon appears on its screen, and goes away when you replace the batteries.
No remote, or it won't respond? Fresh batteries come first. The system can also be reset for manual operation with its rocker switch, with the burner on high only (steps on p. 32). Troubleshooting beyond that is for a qualified technician.

media.title: Caring for the glass media
media.html:
Glass media can discolor or pick up a fine oily film. That's a natural reaction to direct heat and flame.

To clean it

  1. With the fireplace off and cool, remove the safety screen and the glass (see Clean the glass).
  2. Wearing protective gloves, take the glass media out of the firebox.
  3. Wash it in mild dish soap and water.
  4. Drain and rinse it thoroughly. Make sure it's completely dry before it goes back on the media tray.
  5. Spread it back one layer deep, as it was installed.
Keep the pilot clear. Never let glass media block the pilot assembly. A blocked pilot can cause delayed ignition.

Need more media? Your local authorized dealer has replacement glass media. Don't substitute other materials.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building immediately.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Every day

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety barrier in place. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. If at-risk people live with you, an adjustable safety gate can keep them away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. Lint from carpets, bedding and the like can mean more frequent cleaning.

Firebox and bottom latchesYearly · service person
Vent systemYearly · service person
Burner and pilotYearly · service person
Glass inspectionYearly · service person
Glass cleaningYearly · you
Fan cleaningEvery 6 months · service person

The burner check includes looking for gas leaks, making sure the burner lights within 4 seconds of the gas valve opening, and checking for steady flames that don't lift or float.

Between visits, keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, including gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. gives the original purchaser a limited lifetime warranty against defects in materials and workmanship, from the date of purchase.

30 days · parts & laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts & laborAll other parts and material
Years 2 to lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory firebox liner (not enamel or glass panels)

No registration paperwork is needed. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days. Labor is reimbursed to authorized dealers only.

Coverage is void if

  • It isn't installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or isn't installed, operated and maintained as the manual says.
  • The serial number or testing label is removed, or the fireplace is altered.
  • It's submerged, or exposed to long periods of dampness or condensation.
This is a summary. The warranty can't be transferred, and the full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

High altitude

US: above 2,000' (610m), reduce input ratings 4% for each 1,000' (305m) above sea level (AGA derating method). specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
NG min / max5" WC (1.25 kPa) / 10.5" WC (2.62 kPa)
NG recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
LP min / max12" WC (2.99 kPa) / 13" WC (3.24 kPa)
Propane recommended12" WC (2.99 kPa) (Table 7.1)

In Table 7.1 the word "recommended" also sits under propane's 12" WC minimum.

Test at tap A (IN)

  1. Turn all other gas appliances in the house on, or to full capacity.
  2. Loosen the IN tap screw counterclockwise; attach a manometer with a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose.
  3. Light pilot and burner and read. Turn them off, remove the hose, and snug the screw clockwise; don't over-tighten.
  4. Relight and reattach the manometer: the tap should read no pressure.
If inlet pressure is too high or too low, contact the gas company. Only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
NG low / high1.1" WC (0.27 kPa) / 3.8" WC (0.95 kPa)
LP low / high2.9" WC (0.72 kPa) / 11" WC (2.74 kPa)

Test at tap B (OUT)

  1. Light the pilot. Loosen the OUT tap screw counterclockwise and attach a manometer with a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose.
  2. Light the burner and read the manometer.
  3. Turn burner and pilot off, remove the hose, and snug the screw clockwise; don't over-tighten.
  4. Reattach the manometer to confirm the tap is sealed: no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Disconnect the appliance and its valve from the supply piping for any system pressure test above ½ psi (3.5 kPa).

specOpening.html:

For a solid fuel masonry or factory-built non-combustible fireplace installed to code, on a level surface that can support the insert and venting. Smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed if mechanically fastened, and firebrick removed to reach the minimums; cutting the existing fireplace's sheet metal is prohibited. specVent.title: Chimney & co-linear liners
specVent.html:
Co-linear: one 3" exhaust and one 3" combustion air flexible liner down the existing chimney. Kozy Heat #816 has 36' (10.97m) of expandable 3" flexible pipe and the round #816-CAP termination cap. Other approved vent makers: BDM, American Metals (Amerivent), Metal Fab, Selkirk, Simpson Dura-Vent and ICC.

Chimney height10' (3m) min · 50' (15.24m) max
Masonry chimney6" × 8" (152mm × 203mm) min I.D.
Factory-built solid fuel7" (178mm) min I.D.
Horizontal run24" (609mm) max · 1" rise per 12" run
Vent cap12" (305mm) to intersecting walls, overhangs, eaves
  • Exhaust collar on the right; the exhaust pipe has a red marking. Each pipe goes to its correct collar at the cap and at the adapter.
  • Must not share or connect to a flue serving any other appliance.
  • Where the chimney no longer ends at the roof line: approved 4" × 6-5/8" co-linear to co-axial adapter; 10' (3.05m) to 50' (15.24m) total, 24" (610mm) max horizontal 3" × 3" flex, co-axial pipe 1" (25mm) from combustibles on all sides. Cap height above the roof by pitch: Table 4.1 (p. 13), 1.0 ft (flat to 6/12) up to 8.0 ft (over 20/12 to 21/12); two vertical terminations 12" (305mm) apart.

Maker's brochure: mantel 9" deep: 16" from top of insert (11" with Low Mantel Kit). Install to the manual.

The CK34-LMK low mantel kit is for use only with safety barriers CK34-PSF or CK34-RSF.

Hearth (combustible flooring in front)

Option 1: flooring flush with the unit needs non-combustible hearth protection directly in front, at least 7" deep × 33-1/2" long × 1/2" high. Option 2: raise the appliance 1" (25mm) off the floor and combustible flooring may run in front. Safety barriers need the bottom of the fireplace level with the finished hearth.

The manual also prints the 55" ceiling clearance as 1.04m (p. 22); Figures 8.2 and 8.4 give 55" (1.40m) (p. 23, 25).
The manual also prints the 16" start for a 9" mantel as 254mm (p. 22); Figure 8.2 gives 16" (406mm) (p. 23).

conflicts.issue: Metric ceiling clearance: 55" is given as 1.04m in the text of 8.1.2 and as 1.40m in Figures 8.2 and 8.4.
Metric mantel height: the 16" start for a 9" mantel is 254mm in the text of 8.1.3 and 406mm in Figure 8.2.

Glass media coverage: 9.3.1/9.3.2 step 2 says install media onto the burner assembly and pilot shield (propane: remove 50% or more of media covering burner ports), while step 3 says the media must not cover any part of the burner.

Venturi direction for blue/lifting flames: 12.2.1 says opening the air shutter gives short blue flames that may lift, and Table 12.4 says close it for short blue flames; Table 12.4/Fig. 12.3 blame lifting flames on a venturi closed too far (open slightly), and the troubleshooting chart says open the shutter for a blue flame that lifts off the burner.

review.notes: Manual pages 2, 4, 6 and 45 have no text. Not in the manual, so not checked: catalog efficiency (75% NG / 77% LP AFUE) and view area (17 1/2" x 29 7/8"; the manual only gives the 31-1/2" x 19-5/8" glass part, p. 43). Figure 2.1 (p. 9) prints 23", 33 3/8" and 16" among its dimensions but the text doesn't say which is height/width/depth, so the catalog H/W/D weren't compared and the guide doesn't label dimensions. Fan: Table 2.1 lists the fan kit as a field-assembled part, but 11.9.8 calls fan speed control '(optional)'; catalog says fan kit included. Wording problems left out of the guide: 11.9.5 'Turn OFF' repeats the turn-on step (p. 35; the guide uses p. 31/33 for turning off); 11.9.7.3 thermostat deactivation shows two different step-3 sequences (p. 36) and 11.9.9.1 light-modulation deactivation stops after step 2, so no deactivation procedures are given; 6.7 step 4 says to pull the vent adapter 'back to starting position' (quoted as printed in install step 5, 'Place, seat & level'). Log-set wording survives in this glass manual (9.4.2 'verify proper log placement', 12.2.1.1 'check log positioning', warranty lists logs); the guide uses the troubleshooting chart's 'media placement' for soot. Part-number formats differ: barrier CK34A-FPDSF2 (p. 11) vs CK34-AFPDSF2 (p. 43); control boards CK34G-150 / CK34-G151 (not used). Sealant marked '(not provided)' with #816-CAP (p. 15) but '(provided)' on p. 17-18. Massachusetts sidewall-vent CO-detector rules (1.3) not carried into the guide. Table 7.1 places 'recommended' under propane's 12" WC minimum; Table 12.1 gives 12"-13" as min-max. Oct 12: the low-mantel-kit clearance in catalog_mismatches comes from the catalog's brochure note, not website.json, so its page note is labelled 'Maker's brochure'. Website rows checked: BTU input, venting and certification match the manual; viewing area, ceramic glass and efficiency are not in the manual.
